corrected_value.title_o: Social Salience Discriminates Learnability of Contextual Cues in an Artificial Language

decisions.quote: In this study, we investigated the learning of indexical features by English-speaking adults using a novel experimental paradigm. In a conceptual replication of Rácz, Hay, and Pierrehumbert (2017), participants learned an allomorphy pattern cued by a given social context. The social contexts were represented by conversation partners who differed by age, ethnicity, and/or gender and were positioned in various ways.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding (target 0) identify Rácz, Hay, and Pierrehumbert (2017), 'Social salience discriminates learnability of contextual cues in an artificial language' (DOI: 10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00051, listed in References at L670), which the Abstract (L126), Method (L215-L222), and Discussion (L370-L371) explicitly state is the target of this conceptual replication.

decisions.quote: In summary, a larger proportion of participants was successful at learning meaningful contextual associations (gender, age, ethnicity) than a nonmeaningful association (view). Gender, in particular, was the easiest for participants to learn out of the three associations. Gender-based associations were generalized straightforwardly to new conversation partners, but those based on age and ethnicity were also generalized, but to a lesser degree.
decisions.reason: In Method (L222), the authors state that Rácz et al. (2017) found that the socially salient gender distinction was learned and generalized much more easily than the nonmeaningful view (spatial orientation) distinction. In the present study, the authors confirm that meaningful social cues (especially gender, which reached ceiling accuracy and complete generalization across familiar and unfamiliar partners) are learned and generalized better than the nonmeaningful view cue (L127, L340-L343, L357, L370-L371). The intermediate generalization observed for the newly added age and ethnicity cues is an extension rather than a failure of the original finding. Both shipped and blind coding rightly classify the outcome as successful.

decisions.reason: The study collects new experimental data from additional participant batches across 10 new cue/pattern conditions (analyzed alongside the 2 conditions from the 2017 study, L256, L281-L292, L299) in a conceptual replication testing whether social salience governs the learnability and generalization of contextual cues in an artificial language. Note that the blind coding's record_type_quote comes from a portion of the article not present in the stored text snapshot, whereas L126 in the Abstract directly establishes the conceptual replication in the primary text.
